experts.name: Andrew Kappel
experts.title: Principal, LeaderLev Consulting
experts.headline: Connecting strategy with execution to grow better. Sales and CRM consulting for complex B2B.
experts.bio: Andrew Kappel runs LeaderLev Consulting, where he works with complex B2B businesses on sales and CRM: benchmarking where they are, defining what good would look like, and then getting it built, with more deals, better conversion and shorter cycles as the measure. He is also COO of Trust2Connect, a business verification startup automating onboarding and monitoring for financial institutions that serve small businesses. A two-time podcaster, marathoner and former MLB employee, his skills encode the daily habits behind a relationship-led pipeline rather than a campaign-led one.

experts.name: Bailey Darling
experts.title: Co-Founder, Gia
experts.headline: Building the AI knowledge layer for boutique professional services firms, and running the GTM that sells it.
experts.bio: Bailey Darling co-founded Gia, where boutique professional services firms turn their own playbooks and methodologies into a knowledge system their clients can use directly. He runs the go-to-market side himself, which means the pipeline, the demos, the activation and the weekly numbers all pass through him. Before Gia he worked in demand generation at LeadSift, which is where most of his agency network comes from. His skills encode the parts of a founder-led motion that have to run on a fixed cadence to work at all.

experts.name: Chris DuBois
experts.title: Founder and Coach, Dynamic Agency OS
experts.headline: I help sub-$1M agencies stop depending on referrals with positioning so clear it does the selling for them.
experts.bio: Chris DuBois coaches founders of sub-$1M agencies on positioning, messaging and offers, so new work keeps coming in during their busiest delivery weeks instead of depending on referrals. His skills encode how he edits and reviews agency copy: cutting short-form copy down to one sharp claim, and reading a finished page as the real buyer to find where trust breaks.

experts.name: Christian Beck
experts.title: COO and Managing Partner, Five Four
experts.headline: The founder's co-founder. Strategy, brand, and product design for early-stage SaaS.
experts.bio: Christian Beck spent eight years as a UX designer inside large software companies, then nine helping build a design agency that worked with hundreds of startups, where he built the design teams and oversaw sales, marketing and capital partnerships. He is now COO and Managing Partner at Five Four in Indianapolis, the brand and marketing team early-stage B2B founders hire instead of making a senior creative hire they cannot yet afford. Much of his current work is on scaling brand assets with AI inside the tools clients already own, so the work stays usable after the engagement ends. His skills encode the production routines behind that: the small, repeatable pieces of agency output that should never be designed twice.

experts.name: Garrett Jestice
experts.title: Founder and GTM Advisor, 10x Solo
experts.headline: I help booked-out consultants and fractionals grow revenue without adding hours: one client type, one offer, sold on repeat.
experts.bio: Garrett Jestice advises full-time B2B consultants, fractionals and micro-agency owners on offer-market fit: building one repeatable offer around one kind of client, instead of quoting every project from scratch. He spent a decade in B2B software marketing, as Head of Marketing at Lucidpress and then CMO at Eddy, before going solo as a fractional CMO and hitting the same ceiling he now helps clients break. He runs 10x Solo, a private community for experienced B2B service providers, and publishes a weekly newsletter on how solo firms find and keep the right clients. His skills encode the parts of that work he runs on a fixed cadence, starting with how he turns a week of client and prospect calls into content worth publishing.

experts.name: Gary Magnone
experts.title: Fractional Operations Leader, Highrise
experts.headline: I help agency leadership teams align on growth priorities and build the execution capacity to make them move.
experts.bio: Gary Magnone has spent 15+ years on the agency side across strategy, delivery, accounts, operations and growth, and now works as a fractional operator embedded with agency leadership teams. His skills encode how he runs the conversations that turn a vague "delivery is painful" into one quantified problem, a price the owner has already justified, and a booked next step.

experts.name: R. Hunter Harris
experts.title: Founder, Hunter Software Consulting
experts.headline: I help non-technical B2B SaaS founders turn product-tech spend into revenue and growth, with the team they already have.
experts.bio: R. Hunter Harris is a fractional CPTO with 12+ years of engineering leadership in B2B SaaS and four exits (Silverpop, Salesloft, Calendly, Sendoso). He writes the Don't SaaS Me newsletter (https://hunter-software-consulting.beehiiv.com/) and hosts the Build & Break Through podcast (https://www.youtube.com/@BuildandBreakThroughPodcast). He runs his own LinkedIn outreach and CRM with AI agents, and his skills here are the small, tested procedures those agents run every week, with the failures that shaped them written in.

experts.name: Jay Dingwall
experts.title: CEO and Founder, FamousFolks
experts.headline: Your brand and your business are out of sync. I help close the gap.
experts.bio: Jay Dingwall has run FamousFolks, a Toronto strategic creative consultancy, since 2006, working with growth-stage B2B SaaS companies whose brand and messaging have fallen behind the product they have built. The firm covers positioning, rebrands, campaigns, sales enablement and experience design under one roof, which puts Jay in the account conversations where existing clients turn into larger ones. An MBA-educated strategist with two decades in branding and entrepreneurship, he is currently focused on the systems behind the consultancy itself: pipeline, process, and making good work convert into predictable growth. His skills encode how he reads an existing account for the work it should already be buying.

experts.name: Kayla Bonnette
experts.title: Co-Founder, Outlandish
experts.headline: Co-Founder at Outlandish. Scaling the brands of tomorrow.
experts.bio: Kayla Bonnette co-founded Outlandish, a creative agency built around taking brave brands past the ordinary, pairing storytelling with the performance side of digital. The agency's work spans marketing and content strategy, video, social, performance marketing, packaging design and email, for consumer brands including Nike, Feastables, Magic Spoon and TikTok. Her skills encode the parts of that work that have to hold up in front of a client: auditing an account honestly, sizing what is actually at stake, and making the case in a way a founder can check.

experts.name: Paul Munro
experts.title: Founder, AppliedGTM
experts.headline: Helping sales leaders build frontline managers who coach, while most AI sales tools bet on automating around them.
experts.bio: Paul Munro coaches the frontline sales managers at growing B2B companies, one manager at a time, on the argument that the best seller on the floor gets handed a team and is never taught the job. Before that: Salesforce, then Clio, where he ran sales from about $50M through the $100M mark, then VP of Sales at Intiveo, then Head of Sales at EvenUp, where he grew ARR from $10M to $28M in nine months and the team from 4 AEs to 35 people. He founded Applied GTM Strategies in 2024 to do this work independently. His skills encode how he runs a coaching engagement: what he walks into each session with, and how every deal movement gets recorded.

experts.name: Robert Kaminski
experts.title: Co-Founder and Partner, Fletch PMM
experts.headline: I help early-stage B2B SaaS founders position and explain their product so buyers understand it in one read.
experts.bio: Robert Kaminski co-founded Fletch PMM, a product marketing practice working with early-stage B2B SaaS companies on positioning and messaging. His work focuses on the gap between what a product does and how its buyers describe the problem it solves, and on reading sales conversations as market evidence rather than as pipeline notes.

experts.name: Tanyo Gochev
experts.title: Co-Founder & Head of GTM, The Demand Department
experts.headline: I help B2B founders build outbound that books sales calls, with cold email, LinkedIn outreach and LinkedIn content run as one system.
experts.bio: Tanyo Gochev is Co-Founder and Head of GTM at The Demand Department, which builds outbound systems for B2B companies: cold email, LinkedIn outreach and LinkedIn content run together. His skills encode the parts of that work he does every week: writing outreach a busy buyer can read in one pass, using LinkedIn posts to build relationships with founders in his market, and working a revenue goal back into a weekly outreach number.

experts.name: Tony Dowling
experts.title: Director, CONVRG
experts.headline: I fix founder-led B2B sales teams with forward commercial maths, a management rhythm and the Four Pillars sales operating system.
experts.bio: Tony Dowling has spent three decades selling and running sales teams, and now leads the sales-transformation side of CONVRG, a HubSpot adoption specialist for founder-led B2B firms. He created the Four Pillars framework, which sets how a business should sell and how its managers coach and enforce that standard. His skills encode the daily and weekly mechanics of that system: the targeting angles, the 15-minute diagnostic call, the Friday reconciliation, the 80/55/35 coverage maths, and the interview that stops a manager hiring a professional interviewee.

skills.title: Activity incentive sprint
skills.description: Use this skill when a sales team's pattern needs interrupting for a few days: Call 1 bookings have dried up, presentations have stalled, a dormant list needs clearing, or the quarter needs a jolt. Produces an Executive Sprint Brief for a 1-day blitz, 3-day push or 2-week sprint, with targets worked from the team's real baseline, qualifying criteria, a scoreboard, a reward and three daily huddle prompts. Also use for "sales blitz", "sprint incentive", "spiff", "activity competition", "get the team booking meetings this week".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Buyer read
skills.description: Use this skill when a finished page, deck, or piece of client copy is about to go to the client or be published, and a real ICP or buyer research document exists. Produces a ranked list of what would make the target buyer stop trusting it, read in character, with every finding citing a line in a real source, plus what to cut and a score. Catches what craft reviews miss: scenarios that can't happen in the buyer's week, an offer never plainly stated, missing price, unused proof, seller vocabulary. Also use for "/buyer-read", "review this as the buyer", "have the ICP look at this", "what would a CFO think of this page", "be hypercritical about this copy". Not for grammar or voice checks, and never for rewriting.
skills.creator: chris-dubois

skills.title: Call topic mining
skills.description: Use this skill once a quarter, when the content plan needs to come from what buyers and clients actually ask rather than from a brainstorm. Produces a ranked list of recurring topics, each with the count of independent calls behind it, where in the buying cycle it comes up, and the one asset that should answer it. Also use for "what should we write about next quarter", "what do prospects keep asking", "content plan from our calls", "which objections keep killing deals".
skills.creator: christian-beck

skills.title: Candidate interview coach
skills.description: Use this skill when a sales manager is about to interview a salesperson, has just finished one, or is about to make an offer. Three modes: /prep turns a CV or LinkedIn profile into red flags, forensic commercial-maths questions, a 45-second cold-call roleplay and accountability probes; /evaluate scores interview notes or a transcript on five dimensions with a hire, conditional or reject call; /contract generates a signature-ready Pre-Employment Accountability Agreement. Also use for "interview questions for a sales hire", "is this candidate any good", "sales rep CV review", "accountability agreement", "forensic interview".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: CEO exec assistant
skills.description: Use this skill when the person running a small agency needs to know what the week actually demands, pulled from the project tool and the calendar rather than from memory. Produces a short brief: what is committed today and this week, what is at risk, what the calendar makes impossible, and the three things to do first. Also use for "what's on this week", "am I missing anything", "catch me up before Monday", "what's slipping".
skills.creator: christian-beck

skills.title: Client activation check-in
skills.description: Use this skill before a check-in with a client who has signed but whose work is not yet live with the people it was built for, when the call is about to become another status update. Produces a prep card: the one milestone this call exists to move, where they actually are against it, what is blocking it, and the agenda to send. Also use for "prep my check-in with [client]", "they signed but nothing's happening", "client call prep", "onboarding call".
skills.creator: bailey-darling

skills.title: Client list and stack pitch
skills.description: Use this skill when a rep's account list needs reviewing: a list meeting is due, the book is over capacity, or expansion revenue has gone quiet. Produces a prioritised table of every account with tier, days since last meaningful touch, health status (Healthy, Inactive Alert, Eviction Candidate, Flag On Track, Flag Expired) and an account-specific stack pitch angle, plus a capacity line and the week's 3 to 5 moves. Also use for "list review", "rent the list", "which accounts should Danny drop", "eviction candidates", "stack pitch", "expansion angles for my book".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Client win-back
skills.description: Use this skill when the pipeline is thin and the best available list is the clients who already left, or when something has changed at the firm that makes a past engagement worth revisiting. Produces a sorted list of who is worth reaching, what changed since they left, and a message per person that does not pretend the gap never happened. Also use for "reach out to past clients", "win back churned accounts", "who should I re-engage", "we've changed, tell the people who left".
skills.creator: bailey-darling

skills.title: Commercial KPI scoreboard
skills.description: Use this skill when a sales manager or rep asks how the numbers look for a rep or the whole team over today, this week, this month or the quarter. Produces a six-row scoreboard from live CRM deal data: presentations made, closing ratio, sales velocity, average order value, current billing, and position against target, with a 2 to 3 line commercial read. Also use for "how is Danny doing this month", "team scoreboard", "closing ratio", "sales velocity", "are we on target", "KPI check".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Commercial telemetry coach
skills.description: Use this skill when a sales manager or founder needs to install or run forward commercial discipline: setting up the five-tab telemetry workbook (/setup-telemetry), checking booked percentage, gap and 3x coverage per rep across the next three months (/check-coverage), or auditing whether the workshop outputs and workbook are present and current (/audit). Produces, by mode, a built workbook, a per-rep coverage table with this week's prescriptions on the floor, or a pass/fail checklist. Also use for "target to booked to gap to pipeline to coverage", "telemetry check", "are we covered for next month", "set up the commercial workbook".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Delivery audit discovery call
skills.description: Use this skill when you have 30 minutes with the owner of a professional service firm or agency (an existing customer, a closed-lost contact, or a net new prospect) to find the one client-delivery problem worth building a custom solution or pilot for. Produces a quantified pain (annual dollar figure plus opportunity cost in the owner's own words), a price framing delivered on the call, and a booked next step. Also use for "delivery audit", "AI audit call", "discovery call for a custom build", "scope a pilot", "find the gnarliest workflow", "price on the call".
skills.creator: gary-magnone

skills.title: DemandBird exact-time LinkedIn post
skills.description: Use this skill when an approved LinkedIn post (text, image or PDF carousel) must go out at a specific minute through DemandBird. Produces a scheduled post whose stored copy, time and media match what was approved, confirmed by one read-back. Uses DemandBird's MCP server. "Schedule this post for Tuesday 10am", "queue the carousel", "schedule the week's LinkedIn posts".
skills.creator: hunter-harris

skills.title: Builder direction note
skills.description: Turns client or stakeholder feedback on something already built (a staging page, a deck, a PDF, a mockup) into a numbered change note for the person who builds it (designer, developer, editor). Reads the feedback and the live thing, sorts each comment by what it changes for the user to confirm, finds every other place the same line or number appears, and writes "Hey [builder], [client] went through [the thing]..." with exact old and new copy, grouped by asset, and a closing ask for timing. Use when the user says "/direction", "translate this into direction for [builder]", "help me pass this along to [builder]", "what do I need to pass along to the designer", "write this as a note to [builder]", "[client] also sent this", "create a task for [builder] for [person]'s request", or pastes a client email of revisions and asks what changes. Never sends anything.
skills.creator: gary-magnone

skills.title: Friday reality review
skills.description: Use this skill on Friday afternoon, or whenever a week's commitments need reconciling against what actually happened, per rep and for the team. Produces a Friday Wrap Scoreboard: won and lost, presentations, Call 1s held versus booked, versus target, slipping deals with the reason from call notes, a category per rep (Delivered, At Risk, Blocked) and three coaching questions for each Friday one-to-one. Also use for "Friday wrap", "what slipped this week", "Monday commitments versus Friday", "weekly reconciliation", "who is at risk this week".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Klaviyo account audit
skills.description: Use this skill when an e-commerce prospect or client hands over Klaviyo access and the account needs auditing before anyone proposes work. Produces the findings ranked by revenue at stake, and a filled-in Replit prompt that builds the audit deck from them. Also use for "audit their Klaviyo", "email audit for [client]", "what's broken in their flows", "build the audit deck".
skills.creator: kayla-bonnette

skills.title: Kondo owed-reply sweep
skills.description: Use this skill at the start or end of a day of LinkedIn prospecting, when you need to know which DMs are waiting on you. Produces a short list of people whose message is last, for you to decide which to answer. Uses Kondo's MCP server. "Who replied?", "check my DMs", "what LinkedIn replies do I owe".
skills.creator: hunter-harris

skills.title: LinkedIn export contact import
skills.description: Use this skill when you've downloaded your LinkedIn data export and want your connections, sent invites and DM history in your CRM or contact sheet. Produces upserted contacts plus dated touches, safe to re-run every week. "Import my LinkedIn export", "load my connections into the CRM", "who have I messaged on LinkedIn".
skills.creator: hunter-harris

skills.title: LinkedIn shoutout post
skills.description: Use this skill when you want to publicly praise a B2B founder or company for something they do well in go-to-market, and break down why it works. Produces a ready-to-paste LinkedIn post, a first comment, and a source list for every claim. Also use for "shoutout post", "shout out [name]", "celebrate this founder", "who's doing it right", "positive breakdown post".
skills.creator: tanyo-gochev

skills.title: Mail and Messages contact touches
skills.description: Use this skill on a Mac when your CRM or contact sheet doesn't know who you last emailed or texted. Produces dated touch records (date, contact, channel, direction, email subject) from Apple Mail and Messages, without storing message bodies. "Log my emails and texts to the CRM", "when did I last talk to them", "backfill contact history".
skills.creator: hunter-harris

skills.title: Morning paper outreach
skills.description: Use this skill early each morning to turn a curated publication you subscribe to into warm, specific touchpoints. Produces a short list of the day's stories worth sending, who each one goes to and why, and a drafted note for each that you review before sending. Also use for "who should I send this to", "daily reading for client outreach", "turn the paper into touchpoints", "curate and cultivate".
skills.creator: andrew-kappel

skills.title: Network path mapping
skills.description: Use this skill when there is a list of firms worth working with and no warm way in, or when outbound is the only channel running and the network that could replace it has never been mapped. Produces a path per target account: who in the network can reach it, how strong that connection is, what to ask them for, and the message that makes the ask easy to say yes to. Also use for "who do I know at [company]", "map my network", "find a warm intro", "who can introduce me".
skills.creator: bailey-darling

skills.title: Objection comeback coach
skills.description: Use this skill when a rep has just heard a brush-off ("send me some info", "we already have someone", "call back in six months", "no budget", "I need to run it past the board") and needs the team's own tested comeback before the next dial. Produces a cheat-sheet: the recorded comeback from the team's Comeback Book as a word-for-word spoken script, variants to choose from, a 3-line email version, and a pivot to the 15-minute diagnostic Call 1. Also use for "what do I say when they say X", "objection handling", "comeback for the incumbent objection", "they told me to email them".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: OG image from template
skills.description: Use this skill when a post, page or case study is about to ship and it needs a social share image, and the firm already has a Figma template for them. Produces an exported OG image at the right dimensions, named and placed for the page's meta tags, with the title set to fit rather than truncated. Also use for "make the OG image", "social card for this post", "the preview looks broken when I share the link", "og:image".
skills.creator: christian-beck

skills.title: Pipeline by script
skills.description: Use this skill when a small firm runs its pipeline from its own folder with no CRM and an agent records what happens on each deal. Every movement (a send, a reply, a booking, a decision that changes the next step or whose move it is) goes in through one script command that writes the pipeline row, the activity log line, an archive copy and the rebuilt dashboard together, and a drift check at the start of every agent turn names any row left behind its log line. Produces one Markdown pipeline file (open deals, channels, clients won, closed, and a dated activity log), a generated dashboard whose weekly counts come from event tags, and the commands that keep them in step. Also use for "log that reply", "move the deal", "add this to the pipeline", "close it out", "update the client row", "track pipeline without a CRM", "why is this row out of date".
skills.creator: paul-munro

skills.title: Plain-language copy check
skills.description: Use this skill before any outreach or marketing copy goes out: a cold email, a LinkedIn DM, a follow-up, a post, a landing page section, a call script. Produces the copy rewritten to a 5th-grade reading level, with a pass/fail line for each check. Also use for "make this simpler", "too corporate", "plain English", "reading level", "sounds like a consultant", "would a busy founder get this". Not for sharpening a single headline or tagline.
skills.creator: tanyo-gochev

skills.title: Pre-session flash card
skills.description: Use this skill before every session with a recurring coaching or advisory client, when you need one page to run the hour from. Produces the flash card: why this hour matters, the calls you make before the session, the opening move with the words to say, what the client decides today, the development block they asked for, dates and owners, a run sheet, what is already settled, and one closing line on how to be in the room. Built from the transcript of the last session and the recap you sent. Optionally produces a pre-read beside it. Also use for "flash card", "session card", "run sheet", "prep card", "pre-read", "prep me for my next session", "coaching session prep".
skills.creator: paul-munro

skills.title: Price defence and trade
skills.description: Use this skill the moment a rep reports price pushback on a live deal and has a call or meeting coming. Produces a one-line diagnosis of the real cause (budget, competitor, or procurement testing nerve), a value re-anchor script, a concession trading matrix of three "give X to get Y" trades drawn from the firm's own menu, and a walk-away line, plus a printable takeaway. Also use for "they want a discount", "price objection", "competitor is cheaper", "procurement is squeezing us", "how do I hold the price", "negotiation prep".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Punch-up
skills.description: Use this skill when a piece of short-form copy (headline, subhead, hero, CTA, subject line, tagline, ad line, bio, or short section) is wordy, soft, or forgettable. Produces a sharper rewrite, one or two alternates on a different angle, and a score against a six-dimension rubric, revised until it passes. Also use for "/punch-up", "make this punchier", "make this catchier", "tighten this", "this is too wordy", "cut this down", "sharpen this headline". Not for the body of a blog post or newsletter, and not for writing a page from scratch.
skills.creator: chris-dubois

skills.title: Revenue goal funnel math
skills.description: Use this skill when a founder sets a revenue or income goal and needs to know what it takes each week, or when a weekly review shows the goal slipping. Produces a backwards funnel from the goal down to weekly outreach volume, the actual-versus-required gap at every stage, and the one bottleneck to fix this week. Also use for "how many calls do I need", "reverse funnel", "goal math", "what's the bottleneck", "are we on pace", "weekly pipeline review".
skills.creator: tanyo-gochev

skills.title: Riverside Shorts social schedule
skills.description: Use this skill when finished vertical clips from a Riverside recording are approved and need scheduling to YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram. Produces one scheduled post per clip and platform, each read back and checked. Uses Riverside's MCP server. "Schedule the shorts", "post the clips this week", "fix the shorts schedule".
skills.creator: hunter-harris

skills.title: Delivery rundown note
skills.description: Writes the short note that goes out when someone hands a finished piece of work to a client, partner, or teammate (a deck, a tool, a strategy doc, a spreadsheet, a package of files). Opens the deliverable, pulls the last call with the person getting it, then drafts "Hey [name]! Here's [the thing]. Quick rundown:" with four to six plain bullets and a casual close, plus a short "before you send" list of anything sensitive. Use when the user says "/rundown", "bullets I can send along to [person]", "as I pass this over to them", "give them the rundown on what it is and how to use it", "a handful of bullet points to deliver with it", "tldr I can send via Slack", "brief note to go with this", or "match the bullets you wrote for the last one". skills.title: Sales call debrief
skills.description: Use this skill in the ten minutes after a first call or pitch, while it is still fresh and before the next one starts. Produces the record update, the follow-up written in their words, and an honest read on whether this is real. Also use for "debrief that call", "write the follow-up", "update the deal", "was that a good call".
skills.creator: bailey-darling

skills.title: Sales call market analyzer
skills.description: Analyze batches of intro, discovery, or early-stage B2B sales calls to reveal whether the prospects entering a funnel represent one coherent market or multiple distinct market segments. Use when ChatGPT needs to inspect sales-call transcripts from uploads, pasted text, or connected call-recording sources and extract each prospect's specific job-to-be-done framing, current solution or competitive alternative, persona, and company firmographics; conservatively cluster genuinely equivalent patterns; surface fragmentation and dominant segment signatures; and teach the user how to interpret the evidence without summarizing meaningful differences away.

skills.description: Use this skill when a rep or a manager needs to know whether the next three months are covered: Monday planning, a monthly review, or any "are we going to hit it" question. Produces a per-month table for Month 0, +1 and +2 with target, booked revenue, the 80/55/35 booked benchmark, the gap, qualified pipeline and the 3x coverage verdict, plus where to focus. Also use for "pipeline coverage", "target plan", "booked versus target", "gap to target", "am I on track for next month", "Monday coverage run".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Targeting strategy ideas
skills.description: Use this skill when a rep names a prospect or a sector and needs a sharper reason to call than "introduce ourselves". Produces 3 to 4 commercially provocative idea angles, each with the angle, the consequence of doing nothing, and a 2 to 3 sentence phone opener to secure a 15-minute diagnostic call, grounded only in services the firm actually sells. Also use for "give me an angle on X", "ideas for approaching the Y sector", "what do I say to get the meeting", "targeting ideas", "phone opener for a prospect".
skills.creator: tony-dowling

skills.title: Upsell opportunity brief
skills.description: Use this skill before a review or check-in with an existing client, or when a project is weeks from ending and nothing has been lined up after it. Produces a one-page brief: the one opportunity worth raising, the evidence from delivery that supports it, the price, who signs, and the sentence to open with. Also use for "what else can we sell [client]", "prep the renewal conversation", "this project ends next month", "expansion opportunities in the book".
skills.creator: jay-dingwall

skills.title: Weekly content ideas from calls
skills.description: Use this skill at the end of the week when next week's content is still a blank page and the only raw material worth using is what clients and prospects actually said on calls. Produces 8 to 12 ranked content ideas, each with the verbatim quote behind it, a hook, and two formats to write it in, plus the questions to answer before drafting. Also use for "Friday content pull", "what should I post next week", "mine my calls for content", "turn client calls into LinkedIn posts".
skills.creator: garrett-jestice

skills.title: Weekly funnel review
skills.description: Use this skill on the same day every week to see where new business actually comes from, when the numbers live in five different places and nobody agrees what a qualified call is. Produces one row per week, appended to a running history: traffic and outbound by channel, calls booked against calls held, fit, signed work, and revenue split by segment, with the one thing that changed. Also use for "weekly numbers", "where are leads coming from", "how many calls did we hold", "refresh the funnel".
skills.creator: bailey-darling

skills.title: Weekly site and ad report
skills.description: Use this skill on the fixed day each week when a client's site traffic and paid campaigns need reporting, and the report has to say what to do rather than what happened. Produces a short report: the five numbers that matter against last week and the four-week average, what moved and why, and one recommendation per channel the client can act on. Also use for "weekly report for [client]", "how did the ads do last week", "pull the traffic numbers", "marketing report".
skills.creator: christian-beck

skills.title: Work review
skills.description: Reviews something a teammate or vendor built for a client (a page on staging or live, a dashboard, a PDF, a report, a page revamp) and writes the feedback note that goes back to them. Opens the real thing first, not a summary of it, checks it against the plan it was built from, splits the read into "the good" and "opportunities" ranked high, medium, and low, keeps it at the strategy level, and frames it so nobody on the team feels graded. Use when the user says "/work-review", "[person] is asking me to review [the thing]", "draft of the new [page]. thoughts?", "what's good, what's not so good, any high priority items to flag", "check out [person]'s updated dashboard", "is this page organized the way we planned", or pastes a teammate's handoff and asks what to say. Never sends anything.
skills.creator: gary-magnone

skills.title: YouTube transcript panel pull
skills.description: Use this skill when you need the words from a YouTube video as text: your own episode or webinar to repurpose, or a prospect's talk or podcast appearance to prepare for a call. Produces one timestamped .txt transcript per video. "Get the transcript of this video", "pull captions from my channel", "what did they say on that podcast".
skills.creator: hunter-harris
